introFlavors: Beers go in the cooler. Cooler goes in the back. Somebody argues about whose amp is whose.
Two trips to load the van. Third trip for the thing you forgot. Fourth trip because somebody else forgot.
Last gas in town before the highway. Fill it up, grab a bad coffee, and don't look back.
Map pulled up. Playlist queued. Someone already asleep before the first on-ramp.
The house key goes under the mat. The van groans when you start it. Tour starts now.
Ice in the cooler, beer on the ice, snacks in the seat pocket. Routine.
One last bathroom stop. One last check of the setlist rumors. The road doesn't wait.
Somebody's got the aux. Somebody else already has opinions about it. Merge onto the highway.
Gas light was already on when you got in. Classic. First stop handles it.
Everything fits if you don't think about it too hard. It always fits.
legFlavors: Dawn breaks over a Waffle House sign. Coffee smells like salvation.
A van with too many stickers passes you doing exactly the speed limit.
The radio finds a staticy live archive tape for thirty seconds.
Road construction narrows everything to one nervous lane.
You count seventeen tour stickers on a guardrail.
Heat shimmer on asphalt. A billboard promises a grocery store two exits back.
Rain on the windshield. Wipers on the one setting that never quite works.
Billboard: JESUS SAVES. Someone's drawn a bass clef next to it in marker.
Billboard: WORLD'S LARGEST BALL OF TWINE — 14 MILES. You keep driving.
Billboard: ACCIDENT ATTORNEY — 1-800-HIT-HARD. Three of them in a row.
Billboard: INTEGRITY AUTO. The letters have been rearranged to say ROAST THINGY.
A digital billboard cycles through: FIREWORKS, FIREWORKS, GENTLEMEN'S CLUB, FIREWORKS.
Billboard: GOD BLESS AMERICA and directly below it, BARE KNUCKLE BOXING THIS SAT.
Billboard: VISIT THE MYSTERY HOLE. No other information. No exit listed.
Somebody taped a handwritten BEWARE sign to a telephone pole. It offers no further details.
Mile marker 69. Someone always puts a sticker on it. Today is no different.
A hand-painted sign in a field reads: EGGS $2 HONK. Nobody honks.
Billboard: DEBT? DIVORCE? DEAD END? Call Pastor Mike.
Peeling billboard for a movie that came out in 2009. Still confident about it.

truck_stop.label: Truck stop
truck_stop.copy: Neon beer signs and questionable breakfast burritos. Lot kids trade stickers by the diesel pumps.

rest_area.label: Rest area
rest_area.copy: Picnic tables, vending machines, and the eternal smell of sunscreen on asphalt.

farmers_market.label: Roadside farmers market
farmers_market.copy: Local honey, kettle corn, and a guy selling tie-dye out of a Subaru.

supermarket.label: Supermarket
supermarket.copy: Fluorescent aisles and sale stickers. Stock up on food and beer before the lot markup hits.
